Nothing
NUHTH-ing
n.
Webster 1828 treats NOTHING as noun from no and thing: not any thing; non-entity; opposed to something; the world created from nothing; no importance; no value (Isaiah 41). As adverb: in no degree; not at all. This page fills the KJV-gap word of non-entity and empty hands. Companion pages already treat world, christ, and prayer.

Biblical Definition

Nothing in Scripture is not nihilism and not a humblebrag. It names what a man is without the Vine, what the nations are before God, and what he carries in and out of the world. The Lord will not baptize independent fruit: without me ye can do nothing (Joh 15:5). The apostle will not let anxiety play lord: Be careful for nothing (Php 4:6). Gifts without charity collapse: I am nothing (1Co 13:2). The nations will not swagger: All nations before him are as nothing (Isa 40:17). Birth and death will not let a man pack the house: we brought nothing into this world, and it is certain we can carry nothing out (1Ti 6:7). The dictionary therefore keeps nothing from becoming either despair or a pose. It is the Bible’s way of saying: without Him — empty hands.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster 1828 defines NOTHING as noun: not any thing; non-entity; no particular thing; no importance or value (Isaiah 41); a trifle. Adverb: in no degree; not at all. Compound of no + thing.

expand to see more

NOTH'ING, noun [no and thing.]

1. Not any thing; not any being or existence; a word that denies the existence of any thing; non-entity; opposed to something. The world was created from nothing.

2. Non-existence; a state of annihilation.

3. Not any thing; not any particular thing, deed or event.

4. No other thing.

5. No part, portion, quantity or degree.

6. No importance; no value; no use. Behold, ye are of nothing and your work of naught. Isaiah 41:11.

7. No possession of estate; a low condition.

8. A thing of no proportion to something, or of trifling value or advantage.

9. A trifle; a thing of no consideration or importance.

NOTH'ING, adverb In no degree; not at all.

Key Scripture

Joh 15:5 — "I am the vine, ye are the branches: He that abideth in me, and I in him, the same bringeth forth much fruit: for without me ye can do nothing."

Php 4:6 — "Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God."

1Co 13:2 — "And though I have the gift of prophecy, and understand all mysteries, and all knowledge; and though I have all faith, so that I could remove mountains, and have not charity, I am nothing."

Isa 40:17 — "All nations before him are as nothing; and they are counted to him less than nothing, and vanity."

1Ti 6:7 — "For we brought nothing into this world, and it is certain we can carry nothing out."

Modern Corruption

Nothing is corrupted when emptiness is emptied of the Vine, when careful-for-nothing is recast as non-anxiety branding, and when nations-as-nothing is sold as geopolitics without God.

expand to see more

The first corruption is John 15:5 as a productivity gap. Without me ye can do nothing is union with the Vine, not a missing hack. Independent fruit is a lie.

The second corruption is Philippians 4:6 as a wellness slogan. Be careful for nothing is prayer and supplication with thanksgiving — not a breathing app. Requests are made known unto God.

The third corruption is 1 Timothy 6:7 as minimalism. We brought nothing in and carry nothing out because the world is not the inheritance. Nations in Isaiah 40:17 are as nothing before Him, not before a market.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Webster: no + thing. Verse-cache Strong’s on the quotations below: Greek ou / oudeis (G3756 / G3762) at John 15:5; medeis (G3367) at Philippians 4:6; oudeis (G3762) at 1 Corinthians 13:2 and 1 Timothy 6:7. Isaiah 40:17 tags the following counted (H2803) and later nothing (H657); this page does not mint a leftover lemma.

expand to see more

Greek oudeis (G3762) / ou (G3756) — no one / nothing (Joh 15:5, ye can do nothing; 1Co 13:2, I am nothing; 1Ti 6:7, brought nothing).

Greek medeis (G3367) — no one / nothing (Php 4:6, Be careful for nothing).

Isaiah 40:17 is KJV-verified; the cache tags counted (H2803) and a later nothing (H657, less than nothing). No extra Hebrew number is invented for the first as nothing.

Usage

"Without the Vine ye can do nothing (Joh 15:5)."

"Be careful for nothing; pray (Php 4:6); without charity I am nothing (1Co 13:2)."

"Nations are as nothing before Him (Isa 40:17); we carry nothing out (1Ti 6:7)."
